assignments.note: 2025-03 Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail
assignments.why: MAST failure taxonomy and MAST-Data trace set for scoring multi-agent runs (benchmarks), with an LLM-as-a-judge pipeline that annotates failure modes (judges).
Meta-benchmark measuring 12 LLM judges against expert labels with their failure modes (audit), built on web-agent trajectory scoring (agent benchmarks).
Online-Mind2Web live web-agent task suite (benchmark) plus WebJudge, an LLM judge over key screenshots and actions (judge).

assignments.note: 2025-04 Assessing Judging Bias in Large Reasoning Models
assignments.why: Empirical study of bandwagon, authority, distraction and position biases in reasoning-model judges (audit), with preference for later positions as a main finding (presentation sensitivity).
Benchmark of 1,266 hard browsing questions for browsing agents, graded against reference answers.
Agent-based evaluator that distils context and scores generated code; the judge itself is the subject.

assignments.note: 2025-04 DeepSeek GRM Inference-Time Scaling for Generalist Reward Modeling
assignments.why: Generative reward model trained with Self-Principled Critique Tuning and scaled at inference with a meta RM filtering samples.

assignments.note: 2025-04 Do LLM Evaluators Prefer Themselves for a Reason
assignments.why: Measures legitimate versus harmful self-preference of LLM judges against ground truth across seven model families.

assignments.note: 2025-04 Does RL really incentivize reasoning capacity beyond the base model
assignments.why: Studies what RL with verifiable rewards does to a policy's reasoning (pass@k vs base model); no judge, benchmark, mechanism or game-theory topic covers it, see proposal. | main session: assigned to the new topic 'judges as reward signals' created from this proposal.
An agent that searches the web to synthesise implicit evaluation criteria for judging writing responses.
Reasoning judges trained with GRPO and judge-specific outcome rewards.
Measures how often injected distractors flip judge verdicts (audit), comparing pairwise vs absolute question form on the same content (presentation sensitivity).

Procedural executable SWE environments (benchmarks/harness), with tests generated from commits (generated test sets), and hybrid execution-based plus execution-free verifiers (execution-based verification).
Sneaky generator produces adversarial subtle errors that the critic learns from over rounds (adversarial, self-improving judge), and the critic is an RL-trained step-level critic (trained judge).
Synthesises tens of thousands of task instances by injecting bugs (generated test sets) as task suites for SWE agents (agent benchmarks).
Models oversight via Debate, Mafia and other overseer-vs-overseen games with Elo, deriving scaling laws for debate-style oversight.
Audit of how Chatbot Arena's pairwise arena rankings are distorted by private testing, unequal sampling and deprecations.

assignments.note: 2025-04 ThinkPRM Process Reward Models That Think
assignments.why: Long-CoT generative process reward model fine-tuned on a small set of process labels.
Model proposes its own tasks with a learnability reward (self-generated test sets), verified by a code executor (execution-based verification).

assignments.note: 2025-05 Confirmation bias a challenge for scalable oversight
assignments.why: Human studies of oversight protocols such as showing arguments for both answers (debate-style evaluation) versus plain deference.
Thinking judge trained with GRPO on verifiable-reward versions of judgment tasks.

assignments.note: 2025-05 LLMs get lost in multi-turn conversation
assignments.why: Builds a sharded simulated user for multi-turn evaluation (user simulation) and shows performance drops when the same instruction content is split across turns (request serialisation).
Measures attack success of GCG suffixes against open judges' decisions and justifications (adversarial robustness of judges).
Reasoning reward models trained by distillation then GRPO with Chain-of-Rubrics rollouts.
RL-trained reward models that deliberate before verdicts (trained judges), applied to many candidates via ELO and knockout tournaments (pairwise tournaments).
Studies self-bias in LLM-generated benchmarks and mitigates it by mixing generators, i.e. the quality of generated test sets.
A simulated human-like agent with emotional state that converses with the tested model (simulated user) and judges its social cognition (agent judge).
Benchmark of annotated agent traces with an error taxonomy (trajectory-level agent evaluation), measuring how well LLM judges localise errors, best only 11% (meta-evaluation of judges).
Generative judge trained with curated thinking data then offline or online RL.
Process reward model for web navigation trained on step-level preference pairs (trained PRM), meta-evaluated on WebRewardBench with checklist-based step-level scoring of agents (agent benchmarks).

proposals.note: 2025-04 Does RL really incentivize reasoning capacity beyond the base model
proposals.name: verifiable-reward training
proposals.definition: Training policies with reinforcement learning against automatic verifiers (RLVR, executor- or answer-checked rewards) and what that training does or does not add to the base model's capabilities.
proposals.why_none_fit: trained judges and reward models: no judge or RM is trained, the verifier is a fixed answer check; self-evolving tests: no tests are generated or refined; alternative evaluation paradigms: pass@k is used as a measurement, not proposed as an evaluation method; agent evaluation benchmarks: no benchmark or harness is contributed; adaptive reasoning depth: compute is not allocated per input; preference learning: no pairwise feedback or reward model is learned.
